one_liner: Closed-source Windows x64 sparse direct solver (LU/Cholesky/LDLt) with optional CUDA offload; about 2.9x PARDISO on large SPD-type factorizations.
what_it_does: GSS 2.4.1 is a commercial sparse direct solver for Ax=b, distributed here only as a trial: a Windows x64 DLL (GSS_Dl.dll), a licence DLL and file, a C header, C/Fortran/MATLAB samples and a 2014 user guide PDF. The C API is a PARDISO-like phase split over compressed-column (CSC) input: GSS_init_ld (matrix type and a 32-double settings array), GSS_symbol_ld (returns a solver handle), GSS_numeric_ld, GSS_solve_ld (solution overwrites rhs) and GSS_clear_ld. Matrix types are general (0), structurally symmetric (10), SPD (11), symmetric indefinite (12) and complex symmetric (13); symmetric types take only the lower triangle.
how_it_is_fast: Supernodal elimination-tree factorization in which an 'adaptive task-load-tree split' carves out a subtree of heavy supernodes small enough to factor entirely on the GPU (via cuBLAS), so CPU-GPU transfers stay small, while light independent supernodes run on CPU threads. A dynamic scheduler hands more tasks to whichever device is faster and splits a long-running GPU task to give child tasks to idle CPU threads. The README and the author's 2021 arXiv preprint (2109.14929) describe Q-learning for ordering, task scheduling and pivoting; the 2014 guide that carries the benchmark describes only adaptive scheduling, so how much of the Q-learning work is in this DLL is not documented.
when_to_use: Historical or comparative interest: a 2014-era data point for CPU+GPU hybrid supernodal factorization against PARDISO

Windows x64 with an old CUDA-capable NVIDIA card (compute capability 3.0+, CUDA 5.5) and large SPD or structurally symmetric matrices whose numeric factorization takes tens of seconds; the guide shows 1.5x-5.4x there
Repeated factorizations of the same sparsity pattern, where the symbolic phase is reused and numeric factorization dominates
If you can obtain a current commercial licence from the vendor; the repository itself grants no rights
when_not_to_use: Anything that needs source, a licence grant or Linux/macOS: there is no LICENSE file, no source, and only a Windows x64 DLL
Short factorizations: the guide says PARDISO is faster when computing time is short, and GSS loses on msdoor (1.061 vs 0.424 s), inline_1 and boneS10
General unsymmetric, symmetric-indefinite or complex matrices if you want the GPU path: hybrid mode supports only types 10 and 11
Modern GPUs and toolchains: built against CUDA 5.5 and bundles cublas64_55.dll; behaviour on current drivers and GPUs is not documented
Matrices with more than 2^31 nonzeros: even the 64-bit ('_l') entry points take int* ptr/ind arrays

integration.form: shared lib (closed-source Windows DLL, trial build)
integration.dependencies: GrusLic_de.dll and gss_spd.lic licence files; NVIDIA CUDA 5.5 cuBLAS (cublas64_55.dll bundled) for hybrid mode
integration.min_toolchain: Any C or Fortran compiler that links Windows DLLs (header uses __declspec(dllimport); samples include a VC 2010 x64 project)
integration.platforms: Windows x64 only (this repo ships only bin_64); GPU mode needs an NVIDIA GPU with compute capability 3.0+, GTX 780 class or better recommended
integration.thread_safety: not documented; thread count is set via setting[24] (0 = automatic)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same three-phase workflow and CSC lower-triangle input as PARDISO, but a different API (GSS_* calls with a 32-entry settings array, not pardiso() with iparm), and only the double-precision real 64-bit DLL is in the trial

gotchas: The bundled trial licence file gss_spd.lic contains the string 'Thu Dec 31 10:11:11 2015', which looks like a trial expiry date; whether the DLL still runs today is not documented

GPU hybrid mode is off by default (setting[20]=0 is CPU only, 5 is hybrid), yet the guide says its benchmark used 'default parameters' while running hybrid; the exact settings behind Table 1 are therefore unclear

The header is still stamped v2.3.0 (2012) and its float solve prototypes differ (GSS_solve_is takes a double rhs, GSS_solve_ls a float rhs); the trial DLL list only has the double-precision real build
After a failed GSS_numeric call the samples set the handle to NULL ('must set hSolver to NULL') and skip GSS_clear; follow that pattern, because the handle's state after an error is not documented
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rarely: RSLAB is an open-source alternative that reports faster solves than PARDISO, CKTSO covers circuit matrices against KLU with a PARDISO comparison, and BaSpaCho or PanguLU give GPU-accelerated sparse Cholesky/LU on current CUDA with source. Pick GSS only if you already hold a commercial licence and run on Windows.
verified_claims_summary: Vendor user guide (GSS 2.4, 2014), Table 1: numeric-factorization time only, GSS 2.4 in CPU+GPU hybrid mode vs CPU-only PARDISO from Intel Composer XE 2013 SP1, on a Core i7-4770 with 24 GB, a GTX 780 and CUDA 5.5 under Windows 7 x64. Over 12 SuiteSparse matrices the totals are 315 s vs 904 s (about 2.9x, derived from page data), with GSS losing on the 3 shortest jobs; no harness, compiler flags or thread settings are published.
status_note: Abandoned: the benchmarked release is from 2014, the repo's last commit is from October 2021, and it is a closed-source trial with no licence grant, so treat it as reference only.
sources_read: WebSearch: arXiv 2109.14929 abstract via search snippets (arxiv.org not opened)
